options: Removing duplicate columns from a table
Reducing the number of rows while pulling data from a table
Converting unstructured data into structured data
Encrypting rows before they leave the database
Summarising detailed rows into totals
questions.explanation: Data Filtering is about reducing the number of rows returned when pulling data from a table, typically with a WHERE clause.

questions.stem: Why is a filter mandatory on every query run in the cloud?
options: Because cloud databases cannot return more than a fixed number of rows
Because cloud resources are limited and cannot be increased
Because each query is attached to a dollar value, so filtering keeps resource utilisation to a minimum
Because unfiltered queries are blocked by network security
Because cloud tables have no primary keys
questions.explanation: In the cloud, compute and RAM are a click away and each query costs money, so filtering is the factor that keeps resource utilisation and cost at a minimum.

questions.stem: In an on-premises system, what can happen when someone runs a query without a filter?
options: The query is automatically given more RAM
The query holds onto all the available resources and locks the rest of the queries
The query is billed at a higher rate
The query is redirected to the development environment
The query returns only the latest month
questions.explanation: On-premises resources are static, so an unfiltered query can consume everything available and block other queries, delaying datasets for management.

questions.stem: Why is increasing compute resources on-premises slow?
options: Because a complete buying cycle through procurement is needed, which takes months
Because the operating system must be reinstalled
Because vendors only ship hardware once a year
Because the data must be filtered first
Because cloud approval is required
questions.explanation: Unlike the cloud, on-premises capacity increases require a full procurement buying cycle that can take months.

questions.stem: In which environment do developers have the liberty to run any kind of query, on-premises?
options: Production
UAT
Development, because the data size is limited and static
The semantic layer
The staging zone
questions.explanation: On-premises developers may use any kind of query in the development environment because its data is limited and static.

questions.stem: Which default filters are commonly applied to KPIs on dashboards and reports?
options: Show all history for all locations
Show only data that failed validation
Show only rows with null values
Show only the latest month, a specific location or a particular type of data element
Show only data from development
questions.explanation: Most dashboard KPIs start from a few filters, such as the latest month by default, a specific location or a particular data element type.

questions.stem: What is the process of filtering and cleaning data before running models called?
options: Data Curation
Data Syndication
Data Profiling
Data Wrangling
Data Aggregation
questions.explanation: Data scientists normally filter and clean data before running their models; this process is called Data Wrangling and is done by data scientists and data engineers.

questions.stem: Who normally filters and cleans data for Data Citizens, and why?
options: Data Citizens themselves, because they write SQL
Top management, because they own the data
Auditors, for compliance
External syndication companies
Data Engineers, because Data Citizens use low-code and no-code drag-and-drop tools
questions.explanation: Data Citizens work with low- and no-code tools on their own departmental data, so Data Engineers filter and clean the data for them as the first step of preparation.

questions.stem: Which datasets made filtering a basic requirement for storing and processing semi- and unstructured data?
options: Social media, CCTV and audio datasets
Payroll and HR data
Reference tables and lookups
Data dictionary entries
Development test fixtures
questions.explanation: Since social media, CCTV and audio datasets became vital to decision making, their terabyte and petabyte sizes made filtering essential.

questions.stem: Which chain of consequences follows from an unfiltered query on limited on-premises resources?
options: Data drift and model retraining
Higher cloud bills and automatic scaling
More accurate reports but slower dashboards
Duplicate rows and broken foreign keys
Delayed datasets, delayed decisions, lost business opportunities and losses
questions.explanation: Locked resources delay datasets for top management, which delays decision making, which loses business opportunities and causes losses.
